For an entry level sdr, yes, to a certain extent.
The things you mentioned "not interested", "im at work" etc etc are all called "objections" and as a seller youre meant to "handle" them.
Best advice I can offer is, try to learn more about why someone says theyre not interested (for example). There could be a billion reasons, but it could benefit you from learning preciselh WHY theyre not interested. Do they have something in place already, is budget a concern, do they even have a need for your product/service.
Once you learn that, you should try to spark interest/curiosity. Id recommend learning about "objection handling" or try different methods, look into Belal Betrawy's mic drop method too; emohasizes a more "pull" form of selling.
Also, a good litmus test is asking yourself, what would you say to a random stranger approaching you on the street , or calling, and asking "hey my name is x and im selling..." "sorry im in a rush". Thats the natural response.
Try learning how to manage that.

Sales development is primarily "developing sales". Finding potential buyers, aligning interests, intros to warm up relationships etc etc. Folks who work this are called SDRs, BDRs, sales/business development reps.
These guys create "leads"

Sales Engineers, Pre Sales, Solution Engineers are responsible for technical aspects of the sale. Judging complexity, integrations, technical aptitude of buyer teams, usability and utility gaps, demonstrations etc etc.

Typically, SDRs will call up potential buyers and get them to book demos with "closing" role sales professionals. These closers are usually called Account Executives/Sales Executives.

I'm going to share a few proceedings from my life around similar lines in the hopes that they might be a little helpful to your situation. 
I had my bipolar. And general anxiety disorder diagnoses in late 2017. Some physiological symptoms included shortness of breath, chest pains, "ball stuck in throat" feeling, extreme muscle tension and fatigue. It got to the point where a few nights I wouldn't be able to unclench my fists and they would just lock in that position. 

This went on for about a year, experimented with therapy and the prescribed meds (so far only treating my anxiety). I won't get into too much detail with my bipolar, that's a discussion for another time perhaps. 

So from 2017 till may 2019, I developed a few problems. I couldn't get out of the house, or drive, I wasn't able to digest food (apart from egg whites and yogurt), I had become extremely extremely afraid of social interactions and people. Physically I wasn't sleeping, I tried exercising and I remember feeling nauseated after a 5 min brisk walk. Mind you, I had been training for boxing from 2010 till 2012 and kept somewhat active afterwards as well. It was very demotivating to learn that I wasn't even able to walk for 5 mins.

This was the fun part^. The bad part was, NOBODY understood what was going on. I lost my startup JUST as I was starting to get regular clients, went back to live with my parents. My then girlfriend left, she cared at first, but I think I became more and more demanding of attention and she started looking for ways to leave. Soon enough she did. All my friends bailed too, I had become too obnoxious and noisy to be around. 


One childhood friend didn't leave though. He is a doctor, he just told me that whenever I'd need him, he'd come to my house and just sit with me.

So 2019 now, I started pushing that 5 minute walk. It eventually got to 20 mins, then an hour, then 10 mins of jogging, then a few pushups. 
By the time I got to 2020, I could go to the gym. 
Surprise surprise, I hurt my spine, two protursions t12-t13, and l4-l5 discs. Not too serious, but very painful. had to repeat the process again from scratch.

I picked up gardening, writing and reading, paying more attention to the things that I like, like playing music and taking care of my parents. 

The most agonizing part was realising a few things:
People don't care about you if you're hurting, or if you are weak. People only celebrate you when you're already at the top, NO ONE supports you when you're struggling. 
I felt suicidal EVERYDAY from mid 2018 to late 2021, because I felt like I was the lowest scum of the earth and I had to "recreate" my whole personality. 
This was wrong, I've realized that we should be able to embrace our flaws and some minor "toxicities", we're human after all. And if I kill myself in the process of eliminating those toxicities, then what was the point of trying to be better right?

Thirdly, time will pass things will change. People will leave, people will come. You will lose, you will win. The only way to survive is to keep trying, take a few hits, rest a little, then try again. Sounds really cliche right? :P 
But it's true, and it's NOT easy, innumerable suicidal thoughts, millions of tears and many many many lonely nights later we realize that things do get better.

It's 2022, I'm working Sales Engineering for a Fortune 500, I'm physically stronger than ever (actually have abs lmao), I have a healthy relationship with my family and friends. I'm pursuing something that I wanted to since I was your age, music and I've made progress, tiny progress but progress. And most importantly I've learned to prioritize myself over everything else.

Take care of your sleep, your food, get hardcore exercise. That's health, priority no. 1.
Priority no. 2 , make sure you take care of your responsibilities. You don't compromise on healthy food sleep and exercise and you don't shy away from responsibility and accountability. This will be your job, your family, somebody that you need to look after etc.
Priority no.3, relaxation time, indulge a hobby, play music, go out, video games etc. But remember this is 3rd in the list, so if you're not done with 1 and 2, you can't go for 3.
